name: OptimisticConcurrency
purpose: Compare-and-swap write pattern; write fails cleanly when the stored version changed since the reader last saw it.

invariants.rule: compare_and_swap atomically checks old_version and writes OR raises -- no partial update.
Writer MUST retry on conflict ONLY via the retry primitive (no hidden retry here).
Version is monotonic and gap-free per key (next = prev + 1).
Readers never observe a torn write (read returns value atomic with its version).
read(k) of an unknown key returns (None, 0) -- canonical empty, never raises.

extension_contract: Adopters MAY substitute persistent backends (Postgres UPDATE...WHERE version=$1, Redis WATCH/MULTI/EXEC, DynamoDB conditional writes) as long as OC_INV_01..05 are preserved. Version is integer in the Protocol; non-integer backends wrap in an adapter.
consumption_example:
store = InMemoryOptimisticConcurrency[dict]()
value, version = store.read('user:42')
store.compare_and_swap('user:42', version, {'name': 'Ada'})
why_essential: Without a CAS primitive, concurrent writers either use pessimistic locks (throughput cliff) or last-writer-wins (silent data loss); CAS is the only pattern that fails loudly and cheaply.
alternatives_considered: Pessimistic row locking: serializes writers even when they would not conflict.
Append-only event store: correct but too heavy for settings/profiles.
